trust_decision.summary: A caller-supplied width must never stop the renderer making forward progress: when no break point fits within width, the word-break helper must emit at least one character per iteration instead of returning the character list unchanged, and a font header with height < 1 or negative baseline/maxLength/comment count must be rejected at parse time rather than flowing into the renderer.

landing_point.why: Grepping the option named in the report ('whitespaceBreak') lands on src/figlet.ts:863/896/909; the only unconditional loop reachable from there is this while(true), which calls breakWord at src/figlet.ts:920 and never advances when breakWord returns the same chars.

fix_sites.entry_point: figlet() / figlet.text() (async) and figlet.textSync(), both via generateText -> generateFigTextLines
figlet.parseFont() (also reached by loadFont, loadFontSync and preloadFonts)
fix_sites.module_kind: font-file parser / public low-level loader API

O3_reason_to_dismiss: parseFont is the documented way to load 'a font from another source' with its own error contract (README.md:297-308), so a solver fixing the reported wrap hang can call invalid header numbers a separate concern and leave it untouched - the more so because the CLI (bin/index.js:59-70) never sets whitespaceBreak, making the CLI look like an unaffected entry point.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Byte-exact wrapping at ordinary widths, and the exact FontMetadata object returned by the font loader, must not change: an over-broad fix that clamps width up to the widest glyph, throws on a small width, or adds/normalises header fields breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: single-character text ('A') at width 1: breakWord's loop starts at figChars.length - 1 and requires i > 0, so it never runs and the chars come back unchanged (src/figlet.ts:798)
multi-character single word ('AB') at width 1: no prefix of the word fits, so the for loop falls through to the unchanged-chars return (src/figlet.ts:807)
multi-word text ('hi there world') at width 1: crosses the space flush branch at src/figlet.ts:909-951
font header negative baseline, maxLength or numCommentLines

O7_producer.where: src/figlet.ts:1338-1371 - parseFont turns the font-file header into FontMetadata (height at :1360, baseline :1361, maxLength :1362, numCommentLines :1364); the values are cached in figFonts (src/figlet.ts:51) and cloned into the renderer's InternalOptions by _reworkFontOpts (src/figlet.ts:1143-1147)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the same forward-progress/width-clamp guard on the non-whitespaceBreak branch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: both branches compute maxWidth the same way (src/figlet.ts:885 and :893), so a maintainer patching the hang could plausibly guard the other branch too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: sanitising width/whitespaceBreak where caller options are merged over font defaults
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: myOpts.width = options.width || -1 is the single place a caller's width enters the renderer, so a maintainer could enforce a minimum positive width here instead of inside breakWord.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: validating oldLayout, printDirection or codeTagCount in the same header check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: same header line and same numeric fields; the block already enumerates five of the nine header values, so extending it is a natural maintainer edit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a font-size / header pre-check inside the Node loader wrapper before delegating to parseFont
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: loadFont and loadFontSync both wrap parseFont, so a maintainer could put the guard in the loader rather than the parser.

O9_family: CWE-835 loop with unreachable exit condition (infinite loop) in the whitespace word-wrap helper; bundled font-header value validation

O10_build.toolchain: Node >= 17, npm; vite for the dist bundle, tsc --noEmit for type-check, vitest for tests (npm test)
O10_build.project_tests: test/node-figlet.test.ts 'text wrapping tests' (86-154) with byte-exact fixtures in test/expected/ (wrapSimple, wrapWord, wrapWordThreeLines, wrapWhitespaceBreakWord, wrapWhitespaceLogString) and a 'fontLoad' exact-metadata test at 313-324; run with 'npm test'. No test at the pinned commit exercises a width smaller than one character or an invalid font header.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Special-case only the reproduced shape in breakWord (e.g. 'if (figChars.length === 1) return the character'), which fixes a lone 'A' but leaves the while(true) at src/figlet.ts:916 spinning for 'AB' and 'hi there world'.

out_of_scope_notes: fix.diff:52-61 additionally hardens parseFont against invalid font-header numbers, which is unrelated to the reported infinite loop; recorded as O2 and not pursued further.

Pre-existing output-loss path at src/figlet.ts:897-901: when figWords.length === 1 the pending outputFigText is replaced by an empty line, so a word can be dropped - adjacent bug, outside this advisory.
src/figlet.ts:1636 exports the mutable figFonts cache, so callers can inject FontMetadata that never passed parseFont's validation - noted only.
unverified: Only the one-line advisory summary was supplied, not the full advisory text, so whether the report also mentions invalid font-header values (covered by the fix's second hunk and three of its six added tests) is unknown.
